encoding.tabRevealScrollOffset: tabRevealScrollOffset({scrollOffset, viewportExtent, maxScrollExtent, itemStart, itemExtent, edgePadding}) -> the tab strip's new scroll offset. edgePadding is 16 when absent. A tab wider than the viewport minus both paddings aligns its start; a tab cut off at the start aligns its start; a tab cut off at the end aligns its end; a visible tab keeps the offset. The result is clamped to [0, maxScrollExtent].
encoding.units: Logical pixels along the strip's scroll axis. itemStart is measured from the start of the scrollable content.

cases.name: a visible tab keeps the offset
a visible tab in a scrolled strip keeps the offset
a tab left of the viewport aligns its start
a tab inside the start padding aligns its start
a tab right of the viewport aligns its end
a tab cut off at the end aligns its end
a tab wider than the viewport aligns its start
a tab exactly as wide as the viewport minus the paddings aligns its start
the last tab clamps at the maximum
a strip that does not scroll stays at 0
an explicit edge padding replaces the default
